title: AMD heads into Nov. 3 earnings as the first big AI chip test after Nvidia's record quarter
subtitle: The MI400 ramp, OpenAI's 1-gigawatt commitment, and $13 billion in guided revenue put the Q3 report at the center of this week's AI capex read.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: AMD reports Q3 2026 earnings after the close on Monday, Nov. 3. In its August call the company guided to about $13.0 billion in revenue — plus or minus $300 million — and a non-GAAP gross margin near 56 percent, with management saying it expects sales growth to accelerate in the second half of 2026. Q2 data center revenue was $6.72 billion, up 107 percent year over year, and the segment is expected to more than double in 2027.

The report lands two weeks after Nvidia's record fiscal Q2 2027 — $96.2 billion in revenue, $89 billion of it from data center — and gives investors their first chance to see whether AMD's share of hyperscaler AI compute is widening or holding steady. The MI400 series matters most here: analyst consensus going into the year had the MI400 family generating roughly $7.2 billion in 2026 revenue, with MI455X and the Helios rack-scale platform ramping through the back half, and OpenAI's publicly disclosed deal starts with 1 gigawatt of MI450 GPUs in H2 and scales to a cumulative 6 gigawatts of Instinct accelerators.

This is also the moment the AI capex cycle gets its sharpest read. Alphabet reported Google Cloud up 103 percent to $30.7 billion in Q3 and said 2027 capex is set to top $300 billion. Meta raised the floor of its 2026 capital-expenditure range to $135–$145 billion. Combined 2026 spend across Meta, Google, Amazon, and Microsoft is tracking somewhere between $700 billion and $745 billion. Every data-center dollar either goes to Nvidia, to AMD, or to the hyperscalers' own silicon — and AMD's Monday print is the first clean signal on which direction incremental share is moving.

Takeaway for learners: when an industry grows this fast, the useful question is not 'who is winning' but 'who is gaining share at the margin.' Read the Q3 release with two numbers in mind — data-center revenue growth rate, and the implied MI400 run rate from guidance commentary. Those two tell you more about where AI compute is actually heading than any headline number.
